item.title: Over 2,500 rescuers deployed to mudslide-hit border port in China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-06
GYIRONG, Xizang, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- China has deployed more than 2,500 rescue personnel after a mudslide struck Gyirong Port on the China-Nepal border in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region on Aug. 26, the emergency response and rescue headquarters said on Sunday. The mudslide, triggered by a high-altitude glacier collapse in Nepal, had left 43 people dead and 519 others missing at the border port as of 6 p.m. Saturday, officials told a press conference. As of 6 p.m. Saturday, more than 2,500 people and over 500 vehicles had been deployed to join rescue operations. Drones have conducted more than 1,000 flights, and 5.43 tonnes of supplies have been air-dropped, officials said.■

item.title: High-speed rail links two major revolutionary sites of China's Long March
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-06
Crew members of the train G3998 pose for a group photo at Ruijin Station in Ruijin, east China's Jiangxi Province, Sept. 6, 2026. With the departure of high-speed train G3998 from Ruijin Station heading for Yan'an on Sunday morning, the two sacred revolutionary sites were directly linked by high-speed rail service for the first time. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Central Red Army's Long March. Ruijin and Yan'an, serving as the starting point of the Long March and the revolutionary heartland of the Communist Party of China after the Long March, are located in east and northwest China, respectively. (Xinhua/Shao Rui) NANCHANG, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- With the departure of high-speed train G3998 from Ruijin Station heading for Yan'an on Sunday morning, the two sacred revolutionary sites were directly linked by high-speed rail service for the first time. This year marks the 90th anniversary of the victory of the Central Red Army's Long March. Ruijin and Yan'an, serving as the starting point of the Long March and the revolutionary heartland of the Communist Party of China after the Long March, are located in east and northwest China, respectively. The new train service is the first direct high-speed rail link between the two cities, covering 1,857 kilometers at a maximum operating speed of 300 km per hour, with the full journey taking about 11 hours. It serves as a vital artery connecting eastern China with the city clusters in the northwest, with a host of red landmarks and key cities on the route, including Ruijin, Yudu, Nanchang, Wuhan, Xi'an and Yan'an. For a long time, no direct train or flight connected the two relatively remote cities, requiring passengers to transfer at least twice in Nanchang, Wuhan, Xi'an or other cities, with the entire journey taking 16 to 22 hours. In recent years, several high-speed railways, including the Nanchang-Ganzhou, Xi'an-Yan'an, and Xi'an-Shiyan lines, have been put into operation, significantly shortening the distance between northwest and east China. With increasingly close exchanges between the old revolutionary bases in southern Jiangxi and northern Shaanxi, such as red-themed study tours, Party-related exchanges, family visits and business travel, the demand for point-to-point direct services has been rising steadily, according to China Railway Nanchang Group Co., Ltd. In response, the railway authority optimized transport capacity deployment and opened the direct service between Ruijin and Yan'an. Wang Tao, a researcher at the China Executive Leadership Academy, Yan'an, said, "From Ruijin to Yan'an, the Central Red Army once trekked 25,000 li (12,500 kilometers) on the Long March, braving countless hardships and perils. Today, a high-speed link in the high-tech era connects the two points." Song Xuelin, deputy director of the development and reform commission of Ruijin City, said that the direct high-speed rail link has not only shortened the distance between the two cities, but also built an important passage for economic connectivity. It will boost the development of cultural tourism and agriculture along the route, fueling the high-quality development and common prosperity of the old revolutionary base areas, Song said. ■ This photo taken on Sept. 6, 2026 shows paper-cut window decoration on the first high-speed train from Ruijin in east China's Jiangxi Province to Yan'an in northwest China's Shaanxi Province. item.title: Column: China's role in driving higher-quality development of the SCO
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-06
by Xin Ping The Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) Summit drew to a successful conclusion on Sept. 1 in Bishkek, the capital of Kyrgyzstan. The SCO countries held a substantive and productive discussion on the organization's next phase of development, which produced more than 30 cooperation documents, spanning everything from transport, logistics, and biotechnology to artificial intelligence, energy, and drug control. These deliverables mark tangible progress by SCO members in implementing the 10-year development strategy laid out at the Tianjin Summit. FROM TIANJIN TO BISHKEK China has been central to the SCO story: not merely as a founding member, but as a key contributor to the SCO's evolution. Last year at the Tianjin Summit, a milestone in the growth of the SCO, China and other member states jointly crafted a strategic blueprint for the organization's next decade, ushering in a new stage of high-quality development. This year's SCO summit comes at a time when the world enters a new period of turbulence and transformation, and global governance stands at yet another critical crossroads. Rising to the occasion, and with a view to promoting higher-quality development of the organization, China called on the SCO countries to step forward to shoulder the historical responsibility and steer human development to a promising future -- by staying committed to putting development first and opening up the prospects for shared prosperity; taking security as a key goal, and fostering an environment of common security; putting people first, and cementing the foundation for everlasting friendship; promoting dialogue and consultation, and striving for more equitable and orderly governance. FROM VISION TO ACTION Being an architect is only half the job. China has also shown itself to be a real doer. Over the year since the Tianjin Summit, China's initiatives have moved from papers to projects. Seven cooperation platforms covering green industry, the digital economy, scientific and technological innovation, energy, higher education, vocational and technical education, and artificial intelligence have been launched, generating more than 160 projects. Nearly three-quarters of the planned 10-million-kilowatt additions in solar and wind power have been implemented, while more than two-thirds of the 100 "small and beautiful" livelihood projects have been approved. Also, the action plan for high-quality economic and trade cooperation has continued to support growing trade between China and other SCO countries. On Sept. 1, China released the List of Achievements of China's Actions to Promote the Development of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization Action (2025-2026), cataloguing more than 150 Chinese-initiated documents, events, and projects since the Tianjin Summit. China's contributions to the advancement of the SCO are there for all to see. This year, China brought to Bishkek not only a vision for the way forward, but also more initiatives and projects in support of the SCO development. These include the establishment of a China-SCO port economic cooperation center in Tianjin and a basic education cooperation center in Beijing, the launch of an international AI application cooperation center and 100 technological cooperation projects with fellow SCO countries, and the training of more green industry professionals through China-SCO cooperation, among other things. These initiatives will inject fresh momentum into the organization's development. This is where China's role in the SCO becomes particularly visible. While summits set the direction, regional cooperation is ultimately judged by what happens after the cameras leave. Looking back, the SCO has been an impressive success: what began in 2001 as a group of six countries working together to build military trust along their borders and combat terrorism, separatism and extremism, has grown into a family of 27 countries spanning Asia, Europe and beyond -- representing nearly half of the world's population and an economic aggregate approaching 30 trillion U.S. dollars, and covering fields of cooperation from politics and security to economic and people-to-people exchanges. The productive Bishkek Summit has once again proven that the SCO is a steadfast pillar for peace, a responsible force for openness, and an anchor of stability in a turbulent world. As the SCO embarks on its next quarter-century journey, China will continue to contribute its wisdom and strength to the higher-quality development of the SCO, injecting fresh and sustained momentum to regional peace, development and shared prosperity. Editor's note: The author is a commentator on international affairs, writing regularly for Xinhua News Agency, Global Times, China Daily, CGTN etc. He can be reached at xinping604@gmail.com. item.title: China's finance ministry to inject capital into major insurers
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-06
BEIJING, Sept. 6 (Xinhua) -- China's Ministry of Finance will provide fresh capital to three major Chinese insurers in moves aimed at strengthening their capital positions, solvency and risk resilience, according to statements released Sunday. China Life Insurance (Group) Company said the ministry will inject 35 billion yuan (about 5.2 billion U.S. dollars) into the group to strengthen its operational resilience and risk-bearing capacity while supporting its core businesses and corporate governance. In a separate announcement, the People's Insurance Company (Group) of China (PICC) said it plans to raise up to 15 billion yuan through an A-share issuance to the Ministry of Finance, which will subscribe in cash. The net proceeds will be used entirely to replenish capital. The capital replenishment will help PICC further strengthen its capital base, enhance operational resilience and ability to withstand risks, and better leverage the insurance sector's role as an economic shock absorber and social stabilizer, according to PICC. China Taiping Insurance Group said the ministry will inject 7 billion yuan into the company to strengthen its risk resilience, maintain sound solvency indicators, and support sustainable development. ■

item.title: Asia-Pacific media vow responsibility, champion own voice in AI era
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
* The Asia-Pacific Media Forum opened on Saturday in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, with the theme of "Building a Path to Shared Prosperity for the Asia-Pacific Community: Media Consensus and Action." * More than 400 representatives from over 40 countries and regions, as well as UN agencies and international organizations, attended the event. * At the opening ceremony, 16 founding organizations from China and abroad jointly formed the Organizing Committee of the Asia-Pacific Media Partnership Program. SHENZHEN, Sept. 5 (Xinhua) -- In an age when algorithms have the power to both empower and mislead, media leaders from across the Asia-Pacific gathered in a southern Chinese innovation hub, pledging to uphold journalistic responsibility while championing a distinctive narrative for the region. The Asia-Pacific Media Forum opened on Saturday in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, with the theme of "Building a Path to Shared Prosperity for the Asia-Pacific Community: Media Consensus and Action." More than 400 representatives from over 40 countries and regions, as well as UN agencies and international organizations, attended the event. At the opening ceremony, 16 founding organizations from China and abroad jointly formed the Organizing Committee of the Asia-Pacific Media Partnership Program. Participating guests emphasized that development and cooperation in the Asia-Pacific region depend on the active participation of media. The media are expected to share stories of openness and integration, provide comprehensive coverage of the region's progress and achievements across various fields, and help foster a favorable public opinion environment for the region's open development. RESPONSIBILITY, CREDIBILITY AS CORE VALUES IN AI ERA Artificial intelligence (AI), as an efficient tool for journalists, can also create misinformation and deepfakes on an unprecedented scale, according to Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, chief executive officer of the Malaysian National News Agency (Bernama). "Technology must therefore enhance journalism rather than replace its fundamental values," she said at the forum, adding that accuracy, balance, fairness, transparency and human accountability must remain at the heart of media work. "In recent times there has been a lot of talk about the digital transformation of the media, but at the current stage the debate leads us to ask ourselves how we do this transformation without losing our journalistic responsibility," said Felix Paz Quiroz, general director of the Peruvian news agency Andina. "Technology has allowed us to multiply our ability to report, but trust continues to depend on values that digital cannot replace," he concluded, highlighting the importance of verification, transparency, neutrality, ethics and responsibility. U Ye Tint, deputy minister for Information of Myanmar, also cautioned against the spread of fake and false news in the era of AI, stressing that this makes the media even more critical in safeguarding peace, stability and prosperity in the Asia-Pacific region, as well as in building a stable, peaceful and harmonious society. "Through responsible journalism, quality content and greater cooperation, the media can serve as a constructive force in bringing our peoples closer together," he noted. In July, 29 countries signed an agreement in Shanghai on establishing the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization to cope with opportunities and challenges posed by thinking machines. REGION'S OWN VOICE Aminath Namza, chairperson of Public Service Media of Maldives, noted that while much of the narrative about the Global South has centered on its vulnerabilities and crises, it is equally important to highlight its achievements and contributions to the world. "Because some of the smallest nations can have stories from which the world can learn," she said. Nur-ul Afida shared a similar opinion. "The Asia-Pacific is more than a collection of crises, disputes and economic statistics. It is home to diverse histories, cultures, aspirations and human stories that deserve to be understood," she said. To better tell the region's stories, Virgandhi Prayudantoro, chief editor of Indonesia's national news agency LKBN Antara, stressed the importance of cooperation. "Together, we can deepen media cooperation through joint reporting initiatives, collaborative learning, and regional knowledge-sharing, providing a robust platform for intellectual exchange and support for APEC members," he said. Under its Asia-Pacific media partnership framework, Xinhua News Agency has launched a training program for 100 Asia-Pacific media professionals this year, offering immersive sessions on China's media integration, AI applications, AIGC content creation and urban dissemination innovation. Consensus should be translated into practical action through the exchange of news content and professional experience, joint reporting projects, expanded exchange programs for young journalists, regional fact-checking networks, and the ethical use of AI, said U Ye Tint. China will host the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen in November this year, which will mark the country's third hosting of the event following Shanghai in 2001 and Beijing in 2014. This year marks the APEC "China Year," with the theme of "Building an Asia-Pacific Community to Prosper Together." Approximately 300 APEC-related meetings and events will take place in multiple Chinese cities throughout the year. Adjacent to Hong Kong, Shenzhen was one of China's first special economic zones and has since evolved, over four decades, into a global hub for innovation and advanced manufacturing. (Video reporters: Shang Yang, Zheng Qingbin, Zhou Yang, Zhao Tianlin, Li Jiale, Wang Ruiping, Huo Siying, Huang Guobao, Fang Kuan, Mei Yuanlong, Jiang Sai, Wang Hongda, Hao Xiaojiang, Cui Jian and Zou Jianbo; Video editors: Zhou Yang, Zheng Qingbin, Wei Yin and Liang Wanshan) ■

item.title: Xinhua Communication Effectiveness Evaluation Index System releases report on APEC narratives
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-05
SHENZHEN, Sept. 5 (Xinhua) -- Xinhua Communication Effectiveness Evaluation Index System on Saturday released Chinese and English versions of a report providing insights into APEC narratives at the Asia-Pacific Media Forum held in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province. Titled Sharing Inspiring Asia-Pacific Stories, Contributing China's Constructive Solutions -- Insights into APEC Narratives Based on the Asia-Pacific Communication Index, the report was compiled based on multilingual data resources and intelligent research and analysis technologies of the Xinhua Communication Effectiveness Evaluation Index System. The report takes the period from 2023 to the first half of 2026 as the research cycle and selects over 200,000 pieces of information samples disseminated by more than 200 mainstream media outlets in the Asia-Pacific region. In the report, a quantitative assessment system based on four dimensions, namely communication heat, communication breadth, communication depth, and communication attitude, is established to assess the communication effect of the APEC concept across the region, identify narrative characteristics and communication patterns among Asia-Pacific media outlets, and objectively present public opinion trends and the evolution of Asia-Pacific cooperation under the new situation. The report notes that the communication model of APEC topics is undergoing profound changes, gradually shifting from the "annual meeting event-based communication" to "regular value-based discussion." The shift responds to the common aspirations of all economies to seek development, effectively consolidating long-term regional cooperation consensus and promoting widespread dissemination of the Asia-Pacific community vision. According to the report, openness, innovation and cooperation have emerged as the main themes of APEC communication. Among them, in-depth interpretations of "openness" account for the largest share; "innovation"-related topics lead in growth rate; and "cooperation" has the broadest reach and the strongest foundation of regional consensus. The three themes reinforce one another, continuously building consensus on regional development and creating a favorable international public opinion environment for building the Asia-Pacific community. Given the complex regional environment, the report stresses that deepening synergies and consolidating communication efforts of media outlets across the region are of great practical significance. China will continue to deepen dialogue and cooperation with Asia-Pacific economies, build bridges for mutual trust and communication, and work with Asia-Pacific media outlets to tell the Asia-Pacific stories of openness and inclusiveness, innovation-driven development, and win-win cooperation, contributing to the sustainable prosperity of the Asia-Pacific region. ■

item.title: Xi urges greater efforts to nurture capable young people for socialist cause
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-04
BEIJING, Sept. 4 (Xinhua) -- Congratulating a popular national children's radio program on its 70th anniversary, Chinese President Xi Jinping urged professionals in children's culture to redouble efforts in nurturing a new generation of capable young people for the socialist cause. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the call in a congratulatory letter sent Friday to China Media Group's program named Xiaolaba, or Little Trumpet. He praised the program's 70-year commitment to "telling good stories to children," which have accompanied generations of young listeners as they grew up. Xi called on the program's team and professionals in children's culture to fulfill the mission of fostering virtue through education, keep pace with the times, tap deeply into the rich cultural resources, and devote themselves to creating more excellent and popular works that promote the true, the good and the beautiful among children. He urged greater efforts to nurture a new generation of capable young people with sound moral grounding, intellectual ability, physical vigor, aesthetic sensibility, and labor skills, who will be able to contribute to and carry forward the socialist cause. Launched on Sept. 4, 1956, Xiaolaba is the first radio program in the People's Republic of China dedicated to preschool children. It has since grown into a flagship program spanning radio, television, new media and in-school broadcasting. ■
